title: Perplexity launches privacy-minded 'hybrid compute' AI feature for Mac
content:
Aside from being featured by Apple in the M6 Mac mini launch, Perplexity has been relatively quiet on the Mac front this summer. That changes today with hybrid compute for Mac.
Perplexity first announced work on splitting AI tasks between local and cloud models in June. Today, Hybrid Compute is launching as part of Perplexity’s Mac app.
“Computer now splits a task between cloud models and a local model on your Mac,” the company says.
“Computer starts each task in the cloud. Trigger one from your iPhone, and your Mac accesses your files and runs sensitive steps locally.”
Perplexity’s website explains how the new feature works:
Our on-device PII classifier reads each task on the Mac before it is sent. Names, addresses, and account numbers are swapped for stand-ins, then restored when the answer returns.
We’ve open-sourced the on-device PII classifier, trained in collaboration with Perplexity’s Secure Intelligence Institute.
Macs with 8GB and 16GB RAM won’t be able to run hybrid compute, according to Perplexity. 24GB memory is the minimum, and 32GB is recommended as the floor:
Hybrid Compute runs on Apple silicon, macOS 15+ — 24 GB unified memory minimum, 32 GB for best results. Set up the local model once: download PPLX Qwen 3.8 27B in one click. No Ollama or manual runtime setup. Work it handles uses no cloud credits. No API key.
MacStories also has coverage of the new Perplexity feature today. You can learn more from Perplexity’s announcement page here.
Hybrid compute is just the latest AI tool from Perplexity that takes advantage of the power of the Mac. In May, the company overhauled its Mac app with a whole new version. Apple specifically cites Perplexity Personal Computer as a productivity use case for the new M6 Mac mini as well.

report.summary: Perplexity's Mac app now splits AI tasks between cloud and local models, protecting personal data via an on-device PII classifier; requires 24GB RAM.
report.background: Perplexity first teased hybrid compute in June 2026 as a way to balance cloud AI power with local privacy. It now launches in the company's Mac app, which was overhauled in May. The feature starts each task in the cloud, then uses a local model on the Mac to handle sensitive steps. A key component is an on-device PII classifier — trained with Perplexity's Secure Intelligence Institute and open-sourced — that replaces names, addresses, and account numbers with placeholders before data leaves the machine, then restores them in the final answer. Hybrid Compute runs on Apple silicon with macOS 15+, requiring at least 24GB unified memory (32GB recommended). The bundled local model, PPLX Qwen 3.8 27B, downloads in one click with no Ollama setup, API key, or cloud credit consumption. Apple has also highlighted Perplexity as a key AI productivity use case for the M6 Mac mini.
key_points: Hybrid Compute splits each task between cloud and local processing: the cloud starts the task, while the Mac accesses your files and runs sensitive operations locally. This gives you the convenience of cloud AI without exposing all your data to remote servers.

A built-in, open-sourced PII classifier automatically detects personal information — like names, addresses, and account numbers — and swaps it for stand-ins before anything is sent to the cloud. The original values are restored when the answer returns, keeping sensitive details private.

The feature only works on Macs with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later, with a hard minimum of 24GB of unified memory and 32GB recommended. That means many older or entry-level Macs with 8GB or 16GB RAM cannot use hybrid compute.

Setup is deliberately simple: you download the PPLX Qwen 3.8 27B local model with one click. There is no need for Ollama, manual runtime configuration, an API key, or cloud credits for the work it handles, lowering the barrier for less technical users.

Perplexity is betting on local-first AI as a differentiator, and Apple's spotlight on Perplexity for the M6 Mac mini signals growing alignment between AI assistants and Apple's on-device processing push.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Perplexity's hybrid compute is a notable step toward practical privacy-preserving inference, showing how to combine cloud-scale models with local sensitivity. The open-sourced PII classifier could become a building block for other apps. For developers, it demonstrates a smooth UX for local model deployment — one-click setup, no runtime complexity — but the 24GB RAM requirement limits the audience to high-end Macs. For regular users, the payoff is more privacy and no per-query cloud costs, but only those with newer, high-memory Macs can take advantage. This may push competitors like OpenAI and Google to offer stronger on-device options or hybrid tiers, especially as Apple continues to emphasize local processing.
report.tools: If you want to try it, update Perplexity for Mac and download the PPLX Qwen 3.8 27B model through the app. Developers should watch Perplexity's GitHub for the open-sourced on-device PII classifier, and Apple's Foundation Models framework for building with on-device ML. Ollama remains useful for running other local models, though this feature doesn't require it.
